description:

description:
Martin Necas reaches 100 points.  
Late in the third period with the net empty, Necas picked up the puck in his own zone and delivered a clean breakout pass. That assist on the empty-net goal gave him his 100th point of the 2025-26 season — the first time he’s hit the century mark in his NHL career.  
Necas finished the night with the milestone in a 3-1 Avalanche road win, wrapping up a tremendous campaign of 38 goals and 62 assists through 78 games.

description:
In a milestone-filled stretch, Patrick Kane scored twice to reach the 500-goal plateau — becoming just the fifth United States-born player to accomplish the feat and the 50th player in NHL history to do so.  
Goal No. 499 came in the final minute of the first period, as Kane cashed in on a 5-on-3 power play for the Red Wings. Then in the third, with the home crowd in Detroit on its feet, he sent an empty-netter into the cage to secure career goal No. 500 and put the game away.  
The milestone tally came just weeks before Kane later surpassed Mike Modano for the most points in NHL history by a U.S.-born player — two landmark moments in a season that further cemented his legacy as one of the greatest American players the game has ever seen.

description:
Leon Draisaitl made history as the first German-born player in NHL history to reach 1,000 career points, earning the milestone with an assist on Zach Hyman’s power-play goal that opened the scoring. description:
In the second period against the Islanders, Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki took a feed from close range and snapped home his 29th goal of the season at 15:56, breaking the ice in what turned into a 4-1 Montreal victory. That tally pushed the center to his 100th point of the 2025-26 campaign, the first time he has ever reached the century mark in his NHL career.  
Suzuki added an assist just moments later and closed the season with 29 goals and 72 assists for 101 points in 82 games. The milestone also made him the first Montreal player to hit 100 points since 1986.

description:
Nikita Kucherov became the 101st player in NHL history to reach 1,000 career points, joining Steven Stamkos as the only players to hit the mark in Lightning franchise history. He also became the third-fastest active player to reach the milestone, doing so in 809 games—trailing only Connor McDavid (659) and Sidney Crosby (757). A two-time Stanley Cup champion, three-time Art Ross Trophy winner, and Hart Trophy recipient, Kucherov continues to cement his elite legacy.
